ce_bugs.text: Dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent: the .find() predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId but only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is always undefined, causing google.events.update with calendarId: undefined and silent failure of reschedules/edits for legacy bookings
Same dead-code fallback in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent leads to calendarId: undefined when cancelling legacy bookings, resulting in orphaned Google calendar events after cancellation

Duplicate event creation when multiple destinations lack credentialId: each destination without credentialId fans out to all matching calendarCredentials, creating the event N times for N destinations

BaseCalendarService.createEvent filter pins to first host's calendar externalId, so when called with host B's credential the filter compares against host A's externalId, creating zero events for non-first hosts' calendars in multi-host collective bookings

Team destination calendars silently dropped when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar: evt.destinationCalendar is null and the optional-chained ?.push() skips adding teamDestinationCalendars
Only destinationCalendar[0] is persisted on the Booking, so hosts 2..N lose their destination context in reschedule/cancel/email flows that reconstruct from booking.destinationCalendar
Google organizer email pinned to first host's destination externalId on every host's calendar in createEvent and updateEvent, misattributing events on non-first hosts' calendars
Recurring bulk-delete now executes once per calendar reference inside the bookingCalendarReference loop instead of once, causing duplicate delete API calls, error noise, and potential rate-limiting

Google updateEvent fallback predicate searches for externalId === externalCalendarId in a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the fallback never matches and calendarId becomes undefined, breaking reschedules of legacy bookings without externalCalendarId (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~253)

Google deleteEvent has the same broken fallback: when externalCalendarId is absent, calendarId is undefined instead of the destination calendar's external ID, leaving orphaned Google events when cancelling legacy bookings (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~312-315)

Reference externalId is persisted in EventResult/externalCalendarId even when Google createEvent fell back to 'primary' because no destination calendar matched the credentialId, so the stored reference points at a calendar the event was never created in, breaking later updates/deletes (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:264-266)

Credentials fetched directly from DB by ID in createAllCalendarEvents, updateEvent, and handleCancelBooking are used without validating ownership against the booking's organizer/hosts/team, creating a potential cross-tenant credential abuse primitive if credentialId ever becomes user-influenceable (packages/core/EventManager.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts)

Collective events silently drop team calendars when the organizer has no destination calendar because evt.destinationCalendar is set to null (making the later push a no-op) and team calendars are only collected for users after the first (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1062-1075)

Raw PrismaClientKnownRequestError messages are surfaced to clients in HTTP 400 responses in loadUsers, leaking database schema details (table/field names, constraints) on the public booking endpoint (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~750-755)

Dead fallback in Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent destination lookup: the find() only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making the destinationCalendar fallback unreachable and causing calendarId/selectedCalendar to resolve to undefined when externalCalendarId isn't supplied (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253 and :315)

Recurring-event deletion cascade multiplied per reference: the recurring-cancellation block now executes once per calendar reference inside the for loop, issuing up to K× the external delete API calls for collective bookings with K hosts, risking Google API quota consumption and rate limits (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~415-470)

Fan-out duplication when destination entries lack credentialId: every destination entry without a credentialId triggers event creation on all credentials of that integration type, so multiple destination entries lacking credentialId create duplicate calendar events and redundant API calls (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~370-376)

Silent 'primary' fallback in Google createEvent when no credential matches: selectedCalendar falls back to 'primary' when no destination entry matches the passed credentialId, writing multi-host events to the wrong primary calendar instead of surfacing a mismatch (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~146-150)

Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code because externalCalendarId is falsy in the fallback branch, making find() never match, and calendarId becomes undefined causing googleapis client to throw 'Missing required parameter: calendarId', breaking reschedule/cancel and leaving orphaned Google events

Inverted slug condition in organization create handler sets slug only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true instead of when it is disabled, causing organizations to be created with no slug when team billing is disabled and breaking org routing/URLs

externalCalendarId no longer persisted for the legacy no-credentialId destination path in EventManager.ts because result.externalId is undefined outside the credentialId branch, so booking references are stored without externalCalendarId

Non-Google calendar services (Office365, Lark, BaseCalendarService) ignore credentialId and always read destinationCalendar[0], so collective events all target the first host's calendar, defeating the multi-calendar fix for every integration except Google
Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar because evt.destinationCalendar is null and ?.push() is a no-op, discarding teamDestinationCalendars

loadUsers forwards raw Prisma error messages to the client via HttpError 400 (information disclosure) and changes semantics so an empty dynamicUserList produces a 400 where it previously returned an empty result handled downstream

Dead fallback in Google updateEvent/deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find predicate compares cal.externalId against undefined/null and never matches, so calendarId becomes undefined and Google API calls fail on reschedule/cancel (CalendarService.ts:253-256, 314-316)

Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none: optional-chained push on null evt.destinationCalendar is a no-op, so team members' destination calendars are discarded and events are created on primary calendars instead (handleNewBooking.ts:1072-1074)

New DB calls inside the booking-creation loop with no per-item error handling: a transient DB error in prisma.credential.findUnique aborts the loop without rolling back already-created calendar events, and unresolvable credentials are skipped with no logging (EventManager.ts:337-380)

Unrelated inversion of org-slug condition: IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ternary inverts the original behavior so slug is written when billing is enabled instead of disabled, potentially bypassing the pending-verification flow for org slugs (create.handler.ts:151)

Silent fallback to 'primary' when no destination calendar matches the credential: events are created on the primary calendar instead of the user's configured destination calendar with no warning (CalendarService.ts:147-154)
Error handling in loadUsers leaks raw Prisma error messages to clients in a 400 response and misclassifies server-side DB failures as client errors (handleNewBooking.ts:745-751)

Dead/self-negating fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent: the else branch predicate 'cal.externalId === externalCalendarId' compares against undefined/null and can never match, so find() always returns undefined, silently removing the previous event.destinationCalendar?.externalId fallback (should likely find by credentialId as done in createEvent); same pattern duplicated in deleteEvent

Organizer email in createEvent uses mainHostDestinationCalendar (first destination calendar at index [0]) instead of selectedCalendar, so in collective events with multiple Google hosts the organizer email will be host #1's calendar ID even when the event is created on host #2's calendar

requestReschedule.handler.ts is inconsistent with every sibling handler: it has no user.destinationCalendar fallback, unlike all other handlers migrated in this PR (a copy-paste bug from the original code preserved by the migration)

handleCancelBooking DB credential fetch omits 'include: { app: ... }' and passes the raw Prisma Credential to getCalendar which expects CredentialWithAppName; with appName undefined getCalendar likely fails to resolve the app and returns undefined, silently skipping event deletion

evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) in handleNewBooking.ts silently drops all team members' destination calendars when the base array is null (organizer lacking a destination calendar); also pushing into a shared array as a side effect inside the teamMembers .map() mixes two responsibilities

Recurring-event cleanup in handleCancelBooking.ts now runs once per calendar reference because it sits inside the 'for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)' loop, causing duplicate API deletes and N× the work; the logic does not depend on reference and belongs outside the loop

Google updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: in the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy so the find predicate cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making calendarId undefined and causing canceled bookings to leave orphaned events and edits/reschedules to fail

Logic inversion in organization creation: slug spread condition flipped from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}, so orgs are created without slug when team billing is disabled and unverified orgs can claim slugs immediately when enabled

Booking references lose externalCalendarId for the no-credentialId path because createAllCalendarEvents else-branch calls createEvent with no externalId, so stored references have externalCalendarId undefined and later mutations fail

Silent skip when a destination's credential can't be resolved (credentialFromDB null, deleted, or app.slug null): no EventResult pushed, no error logged, so booking is reported successful while a host's calendar never receives the event

In updateAllCalendarEvents, a failed DB fetch passes credential = undefined into updateEvent which throws in getCalendar, and the outer catch converts all references into failures discarding ones that already succeeded (cascade failure)
Reschedule-merge deletion path still uses .find() on booking.references instead of .filter(), so only the first old calendar reference is deleted and hosts 2..N keep stale events after a reschedule

Organizer email forced to mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId (first destination) for all hosts' calendars in Google createEvent/updateEvent, causing rejected inserts or wrong organizer attribution on secondary hosts' calendars

Video references lose credentialId (changed from result.credentialId to undefined for non-calendar types), degrading reschedule and location edit flows to type-based matching instead of credential-based

Google createEvent silently falls back to "primary" when no destination matches the credential, creating events in the wrong calendar and pointing the booking reference at an externalId the user never chose

requestReschedule preserved the duplicated-operand bug (booking?.destinationCalendar || booking?.destinationCalendar) instead of falling back to user.destinationCalendar like other handlers, so cancellation/reschedule emails carry no calendar info

DB credential fetches in EventManager look up credentials by bare id with no ownership check against the booking's users, a potential credential-abuse vector if any API lets users write destinationCalendar.credentialId

mrv_findings.text: In packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-118, mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty, because destructuring ?? [] yields undefined and there is no optional chaining on the member access — booking a Google Meet event type as a user with no destination calendar crashes instead of falling back to Daily video

In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-256 (updateEvent) and :313-315 (deleteEvent), the fallback branch is dead code because the find predicate cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy in the else branch, causing calendarId: undefined to be sent to the Google API and breaking reschedule/cancel for reference rows lacking a stored externalCalendarId

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151, the slug guard condition was silently inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}, which are logical opposites — with team billing disabled the Organization create no longer receives slug (possible Prisma required-constraint violation), and with billing enabled the slug bypasses the requestedSlug verification flow

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~424-429, the DB credential fallback omits the app include, so getCalendar() cannot resolve the calendar service (a raw Prisma Credential has appId, not appName), causing the booking to be cancelled in Cal.com but never deleted from the external calendar

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1072, evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) silently drops team calendars when the base is null, defeating the collective multiple host fix for organizers without a personal destination calendar

In packages/core/EventManager.ts:~347 and ~505, new prisma.credential.findUnique(...) calls reference a bare prisma identifier with no corresponding import hunk in the diff, potentially causing a compile-time failure if prisma is not already imported

In packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221, createEvent(event, credentialId: number) makes the second parameter required on the Calendar interface while other implementations declare createEvent(event: CalendarEvent), so any caller invoking calendar.createEvent(evt) with one argument becomes a type error — the parameter should be optional or all call sites audited

EventManager.ts:117 crashes with TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty because the null-safe ?. was removed, so mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws for Google-Meet bookings without a destination calendar

Google CalendarService.ts:253 and :313 dead-code fallback: when externalCalendarId is falsy, find compares externalId against falsy value and never matches, so selectedCalendar is undefined and update/delete sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API (missing || "primary" fallback unlike createEvent)

Only Google Calendar implements multi-host destination selection; Office365, Lark, and CalDAV/BaseCalendarService ignore the credentialId/destination params and always use host #1's calendar, writing other hosts' events to the wrong calendar

EventManager.ts:169 sets externalCalendarId to undefined on the no-credentialId branch because createEvent is called without destination.externalId, so result.externalId is undefined and references lose externalCalendarId

handleNewBooking.ts:1071: when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are null, evt.destinationCalendar is null and the ?.push() is a no-op, silently dropping collective team destination calendars; also this is the only construction site yielding null instead of []

Google CalendarService.ts:122: organizer email is always the first host's destination calendar externalId even for events created on other hosts' calendars, causing wrong organizer display or API rejection of the organizer override (same pattern in updateEvent at ~228)

handleCancelBooking.ts:~430: recurring-cancellation loop was moved inside the per-reference loop but still iterates all organizer credentials and all updatedBookings references, duplicating deleteEvent calls and causing spurious 404/410 errors for multi-host bookings
No test exercises the multi-host path this PR exists to fix; the only test change is a mechanical fixture type adaptation, leaving the core new behavior with zero regression coverage

In create.handler.ts:151, unrelated change with inverted logic: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was rewritten to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, flipping existing behavior so orgs only get a slug when team billing IS enabled

In EventManager.ts:117, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` lacks optional chaining even though the PR now produces `destinationCalendar: []`, causing TypeError when Meet-fallback flows reach EventManager.create with an empty array

In googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:253 and :315, dead-code fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match since externalCalendarId is falsy in the else branch, so `calendarId: undefined` is sent to the Google API instead of the destination calendar

The multi-host fix (using credentialId) is only implemented for Google; Lark (CalendarService.ts:127, :164, :192, :237) and Office365 (CalendarService.ts:73) still read only element [0] of destinationCalendar, causing duplicate events on the first host's calendar and zero on other hosts

In handleNewBooking.ts:722-770, the loadUsers rewrite is unrelated to the PR intent and deleted the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` select, so downstream consumers of users' organization.slug now get undefined; Prisma errors also now surface as HTTP 400s

In handleCancelBooking.ts:435-450, recurring-series cancellation still iterates only the organizer's credentials, so cancelling a recurring collective series orphans other hosts' calendar events and fires the organizer's credentials at refs they don't own (404s)

In googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:119-123, organizer.email is set from the first destinationCalendar element while selectedCalendar is chosen by credentialId match, resulting in wrong organizer identity when the matched destination is not element [0]

In requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-243, the fallback pattern is inconsistently applied: this handler drops the `user.destinationCalendar` fallback (uses `: []`) while all sibling handlers changed in the same diff keep it, so reschedule flows lose the user-level calendar

Meet-location fallback in EventManager.ts:117 crashes on empty destinationCalendar — destructured value may be undefined and .integration is accessed without optional chaining, throwing TypeError when no destination calendar exists instead of fallinging back to Daily video, breaking booking confirm flows

Google CalendarService.ts:256 updateEvent fallback is dead code — in the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match, making selectedCalendar always undefined and causing events.update with calendarId: undefined which Google rejects

Google CalendarService.ts:315 deleteEvent contains the same dead-code fallback bug — calendarId is undefined when externalCalendarId is absent, breaking reschedules and cancellations for bookings created without the externalId arg

The createEvent(event, credentialId) interface conveys the wrong discriminator and only Google implements multi-host — Office365, Lark, and CalDav BaseCalendarService don't use the parameter and still pick destinationCalendar[0], so collective bookings write to the first host's calendar using a different host's OAuth token, causing 404s that are silently swallowed

create.handler.ts:151 condition inverted by mechanical refactor — (!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) became (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}), flipping semantics so the slug-approval workflow is bypassed exactly when it should apply and orgs without team billing get no slug

handleNewBooking.ts:1078 evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) is a silent no-op when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are null, dropping all collective hosts' calendars so collective bookings get no calendar events on any host's calendar

handleNewBooking.ts:1078 asymmetry — when eventType.destinationCalendar is set, the organizer's own user calendar is the only entry deliberately excluded while all other hosts are included, which is asymmetric for collective events

EventManager.ts:520-555 unguarded updateEvent(credential, ...) call after a failed DB fetch — if the credential lookup returns null, updateEvent is still called with undefined, and the outer catch replaces the entire result array, turning already-completed updates on other hosts' calendars into reported failures

EventManager.ts:560 merge path deletes only the first calendar reference of the old booking — collective bookings carry multiple _calendar references per host, so remaining hosts' old calendar events are orphaned and stay on their calendars forever

EventManager.ts:340-380 createAllCalendarEvents now awaits createEvent serially in a for loop plus a per-destination prisma.credential.findUnique inside the loop, replacing the old Promise.all parallelization and adding N sequential third-party API round-trips on the booking hot path; same shape in handleCancelBooking

handleNewBooking.ts:688-689, 994, 1077 replace the imported SchedulingType enum with magic strings like "COLLECTIVE" in multiple places with no shared constant, losing compile-time safety if the enum variant is renamed

handleNewBooking.ts:1064-1078 assembles the destinationCalendar array without dedupe by credentialId/externalId — if the event type's DC shares a credential with a host's DC, createAllCalendarEvents creates the event twice on the same calendar, producing duplicate calendar events for attendees

In CalendarService.ts (updateEvent and deleteEvent), the destinationCalendar fallback is dead code: when externalCalendarId is falsy, find() compares non-empty externalIds against a falsy value and never matches, so calendar.events.update/delete receive calendarId: undefined, causing bookings without externalCalendarId to fail to update/delete on Google (orphan events).

In EventManager.ts, the Google-Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback crashes: destructuring an empty destinationCalendar array yields undefined, and undefined.integration throws a TypeError, failing booking creation for Google Meet events by users with no destination calendar.

In create.handler.ts, an unrelated conditional was inverted (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED logic flipped), so orgs on non-billing instances lose their slug entirely and billing-enabled orgs get both slug and requestedSlug set, defeating the pending-verification flow.

In EventManager.ts, the credential variable is declared outside the new reference loop and retains stale values across iterations, so a reference whose credentialId can't be resolved silently reuses the previous reference's credential, running updateEvent against the wrong host's calendar or crashing in getCalendar.

In handleNewBooking.ts, the collective-host destination calendar push is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (organizer has no destination calendar), so team members' destination calendars are never used and the generic per-credential fallback runs instead.

In CalendarService.ts, CalDAV event creation is filtered by the first host's externalId, so with mixed-provider collective events the filter (comparing CalDAV URLs against a Google externalId) yields an empty list and no event is created on the CalDAV host's calendar.

In createAllCalendarEvents (~line 348-370, EventManager.ts), credential lookup by bare id with no userId/teamId/org scope allows destination.credentialId (user-configurable via destinationCalendar) to reference another user's or org's credential, causing cross-user/cross-tenant event writes with the victim's OAuth token

In updateAllCalendarEvents (~line 505-540, EventManager.ts), the same unscoped prisma.credential.findUnique by reference.credentialId lets the server adopt a credential not owned by the booking's organizer and update/delete external calendar events with a foreign OAuth token

In handleCancelBooking.ts (~line 425-437), the cancellation path drops the owner-scoped credential filter: if the credential isn't found in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, it fetches any credential from the entire Credential table by ID and uses it to issue calendar.deleteEvent, enabling cross-user destructive event deletion with a foreign OAuth token

The only test change in the diff is a one-line snapshot update in a BOOKING_REJECTED email assertion (destinationCalendar: null → []), verifying only a serialized string in an email body rather than the multi-host collective fan-out behavior the PR claims to fix — the riskiest paths (per-destination loop, per-credential DB fetch, multi-reference cancel loop, credentialId-based calendar selection) ship with no test creating a collective booking with two hosts and asserting two calendar references

New find() branch in googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:256 (and identically at :315) is provably dead code: the fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but the predicate compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId against the same falsy value so find never matches, making the ternary equivalent to externalCalendarId || undefined — silently removing the previously-working destinationCalendar.externalId fallback so Google API hits the wrong/default calendar on update/delete with absent externalCalendarId

In handleNewBooking.ts:~1077, the team-calendar push silently no-ops when evt.destinationCalendar is null (set when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), dropping every team member's destination calendar without error or log, so a collective event with a null-organizer destination calendar produces zero calendar events for all hosts — reintroducing the exact bug the PR claims to fix

Non-Google calendar services (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128, Office365 :73, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:~156) were migrated to a 'first element' fallback (destinationCalendar[0]) while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination/credential, causing duplicate events on the first host's calendar and nothing on the second host's calendar for multi-host collective events — Google got credentialId matching but other backends only work for single-host, and no e2e test covers non-Google backends

In EventManager.ts:~596, the catch block now returns an empty array when the try block throws before calendarReference is assigned (e.g., prisma.credential.findUnique fails), making a failed reschedule/update indistinguishable from 'nothing to update' and reporting success-by-omission to callers checking results.length or success flags, whereas the previous code returned a visible failure EventResult

In EventManager.ts:~500-540, when reference.credentialId isn't in this.calendarCredentials and the DB fetch returns null, credential remains undefined and is passed to updateEvent(undefined, ...) whose throw is swallowed by the outer catch, so a calendar reference with a deleted credential is silently dropped rather than reported as a failure

Null-safety regression in EventManager.ts (lines 116-118): destructuring evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] can yield undefined for mainHostDestinationCalendar, and accessing .integration without optional chaining crashes with TypeError for Meet bookings with no destinationCalendar (e.g., from bookingReminder.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts, webhook.ts, confirm.handler.ts passing [])

Dead fallback in CalendarService.ts updateEvent (lines 253-255) and deleteEvent (lines 313-315): when externalCalendarId is falsy, find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match, so legacy bookings without externalCalendarId (and new bookings from the createEvent no-credentialId branch) send calendarId: undefined to the Google API, leaving orphaned Google Calendar events

handleNewBooking.ts (~1063-1073): uses null instead of [] for missing destinationCalendar, making the subsequent ?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) a silent no-op, so COLLECTIVE events whose event type and organizer have no destinationCalendar silently drop all team members' destination calendars

Schema drift in handleNewBooking.ts (~1871-1877): in-memory model is now DestinationCalendar[] but only element [0] is persisted via connect since Booking.destinationCalendar remains a single FK with no migration, so read-back flows like requestReschedule.handler.ts rebuild a single-element array and rescheduling/canceling collective bookings orphans events on other hosts' calendars

EventManager.ts (~548-552): merge/reschedule path still uses .find() on booking.references to locate the old calendar event, deleting only the first matching calendar reference and orphaning old events on all other hosts' calendars for multi-reference collective bookings
